qt: to the Commission Marcin Sypniewski (ESN) Subject:

In October 2026, state authorities and animal welfare NGOs carried out a joint intervention at a zoo in Łączna, Poland. Reports emerged of organisational shortcomings, difficulties in providing the animals with adequate care and several deaths among the animals. Some of the animals were transported to other Member States. On 27 October 2026, the public prosecutor’s office overturned the earlier decisions on the custody of the animals, allowing the zoo’s existing management to resume care of those remaining on site. This incident raises questions about the scope of the powers granted to animal welfare NGOs, the oversight of their activities and liability for the consequences of their interventions. In light of the above: 1.

What EU rules govern the involvement of NGOs in seizing and taking custody of animals, particularly when it comes to the qualifications required, the scope of their powers, oversight of their actions and liability for those actions?

Will the Commission consider introducing minimum standards to ensure that such interventions are proportionate, that veterinary care remains uninterrupted, and that responsibility for the animals is clearly assigned, while also providing for the option of leaving them on site under appropriate supervision?

Will the Commission request information from the competent authorities regarding the transport of animals from the zoo in Łączna to other Member States, including its compliance with EU legislation on veterinary checks and animal traceability?
